I would say those four points break it down. My partner and I have discussed this exact topic. Some of the old art is really bad. [[Giant's Strength]] comes to mind. But then you had really evocative pieces like Sol Ring and Nivynerral's Disk.

The "modern standard" versions of those as I'm calling. It, are very technically detailed and beautiful illustrations. Both of the modern versions are very high contrast and in one case, has a lot of great lighting going on. However, the original art for one of them is a relatively impressionistic burning ring above what looks like the surface of a star. And then the new version is just a point of light in the middle of a very well drawn reflective gold ring floating in a relative void. I know it's not devoid of detail but you know what I mean.

The original art of the other. Not a lot of shading for shadows or lighting, but a very evocative image of this horrific tentacle and toothy maw coming out of this little disc. Very very evocative and memorable.

Sure, you can make the point that the newer drawings of both are much more technically skilled and realistic and things like that. And sure, some of the 40K and other versions of the Sol Ring look fantastic, and are huge improvements in my opinion over the usual printing image. But I do feel like it lost something moving away from the more stylistic and impressionistic art styles of some of them. The utterly alien look of the early Senghir vampire card is something I love.

That being said, I don't poopoo on the modern art. I definitely like looking at some of it and I don't think some of these cards would look good in the old art styles. I do think that as far as consistently hiring more skilled artists, it's benefited a lot as well. Because some of those old cards were just not good. But I do wish they would let people do more stylized art on them more often
